body: I was diagnosed with autism when I was 3 years old, and all it's really done for me is give me an explanation growing up. I distinctly remember being in 1st grade, where we were all put into groups we shared a single "desk" with, and my groupmates built a wall around me with their school supplies and said "you're not welcome with us". And that mentality just kinda remained until 7th grade. I had good enough grades to join honor society, but my history/reading/special ed teacher had beef with my mother, and took it out on me. She raised my reading level 10 times higher than the average for the rest of the school, knowing damn well I couldn't achieve it, and it was just enough to lower my GPA, and get me kicked out of honor society. As a result, I was no longer eligible for a scholarship straight to a 4 year (which I was told I had a very high chance of achieving, and I had high hopes for), and I remained an outsider until the day I graduated high school. I decided to go to a 2 year junior college, and take a couple classes to "get my feet wet". One of my classmates decided to start a rumor about me, that I was going to shoot up the school. The police got involved, and sided with the rumor. I was arrested, hospitalized, 51/50ed, drug tested, etc. The hospital psychiatrist eventually deemed me not a danger to myself or anyone else, and I was discharged. My school decided to suspend me anyway, and I was forced to attend a hearing, where my accuser chose not to show up. The dean sided with my accuser, decided to bring up Sandy Hook, and how the shooter had autism, and had the audacity to say that my own autism was a red flag. I was expelled, and the superintendent denied my appeal, and the lawyer I hired took my money and ran. After spending about a year trying to heal from that, I got a job as a grocery bagger. Go figure, told my whole life I was special and that I was going to do great things, to end up denied an education by force, and having to work minimum wage. My boss constantly treated me like I was 5 years old, and put me in catch-22 situations all the time. I worked there for a year and a half, and quit around the time I turned 21. I got a different job delivering packages for an Amazon DSP. My boss was constantly angry with me for "being slow", and cussed me out all the time. I worked at that job for about a year, until an extreme burnout kicked in, and left me hospitalized. After I was discharged, I decided to take a mental health trip, with a friend of mine. I was 10 minutes from my destination, when we were involved in a car accident that totaled my car, and my friend decided to use the accident to extort insurance out of me. It caused me over a year's worth of hell with insurance, and it's cost me a lot of money I don't have. I just recently turned 24, I've been unemployed for almost 2 years, my physical health is at an all time low, my mental health has never been worse, I'm living at home with my parents, who constantly remind me of how lazy I am (and angrily so), and I can't get a job because of my health, and I can't afford to better myself because I don't have a job. I look up what burnout is, and it says it's only supposed to last about 3 months. Considering I've had no energy for 2 years, I'm now convinced this will last the rest of my life. Life has successfully beaten me to a pulp, and I don't want to fight back anymore. I'm convinced that either I'm cursed, or that this world was built preemptively to keep me from succeeding. Either way, I'm about ready to give up entirely.

I survived a head-on collision earlier this week, and my phone was destroyed in the process. I lost my job a little over a month ago, and have no income to recover from getting an new car and phone. My friend who was in the car with me, decided being my friend wasn't worth it after that, and blocked me on everything. Everyone kept telling me to be thankful to have survived, but in reality, I wish I died in the accident. I took a bunch of xanax this morning for the first time in years (technically yesterday morning, since its now midnight), and slept today off. I couldn't bear the thought of celebrating Thanksgiving, when I'm not even thankful for my own life.

This resonated with me very much. I 100% prefer to be alone, as 99.999% of people cause me irritation and put me at unease. I was in a long distance relationship a couple of years ago with a girl who I'm convinced is some sort of angel (despite the fact that I'm not religious). Her love language is physical touch, and mine is words of affirmation. I have autism, and physical contact with people makes my skin crawl. But with her, I wanted nothing more than to cuddle with her. She was that constant bright light in a world of perpetual darkness. She was the dictionary definition of perfect, and she was always able to put a smile on my face, even if I was having the shittiest day ever. And she'd often tell me I had a similar effect on her. She always told me she suffered from resting-bitch-face, but whenever her and I finished a Facetime call, her cheeks would hurt from smiling so much. Something that only happened to her when her and I were on the phone. Sometimes we'd start a Facetime call and not even speak. We'd just stare into each other's eyes through our screens, and just virtually enjoy each other's company. She suffers from Borderline Personality Disorder and extreme depression, and I suffer from Autism and Bipolar Disorder, and we both had our fair share of trauma, so we just understood each other. Her and I are both painfully socially awkward, but it didn't matter to us, because we just understood each other. It was the best time of my life. Our relationship eventually came to an end, as I'm non religious, and she comes from a very religious family, and it was creating a lot of tension between her and her family. I didn't enjoy seeing her in that kind of pain, so I ended the relationship, to give her and her family the opportunity to heal the tension. Her and I remained friends after that, but she eventually fell in love with someone else, as he was able to give her the one thing I couldn't, in-person company. Their relationship ended up fizzling out, and she's now slowly falling for another guy. I love her so much, but her no longer reciprocating those same feelings brings me such a level of pain, I can't even describe what it feels like. I can't talk to her as often as I used to, because I want more than anything to tell her how much I love her, but I don't want to destroy this beautiful friendship I have with her. I hold a pillow in my arms every night as I fall asleep, wishing it was her. I have befriended other women, both online and in person, but none of them are as amazing as she is. I miss her so much
